//: Tracked, so a fresh clone gets this with nothing to install. Both hooks call helm's own CLI by module name and use no absolute paths, so they work in any checkout on any machine.

hooks.//: Arms the in-session watch. A Monitor dies with its session and nothing re-arms it, so a restarted root goes blind until somebody notices -- the exact failure this mechanism exists to prevent. `pending --changes` keeps the loop to one command with no shell state, so the watch cannot drift from what Helm reports.
hooks.command: printf '%s\n' 'HELM: arm the attention watch for this session before anything else. Use the Monitor tool with persistent:true and description "Helm", running: while true; do python3 -m helm pending --changes; sleep 20; done --- it prints ONLY what is new since the last check and nothing otherwise, so a gate, approval request, worker question, blocker or terminal report wakes you within 20s while a quiet root stays silent.'

hooks.//: Prints nothing when nothing needs a human, so a quiet root stays quiet.
